title: Clinton Library onsite research plan from 2013-0185-M finding aids
scope: Actionable pull strategy for Clinton Library onsite work on FRUS 1993-2000, Volume XVIII, Russia. Built from four user-provided 2013-0185-M finding-aid PDFs and focused on Clinton-Yeltsin memcons, telcons, summit files, aide chron files, source-note control, and hard source gaps.

highValueSeries: Office of the National Security Advisor

summary.onsitePriority: Start with direct memcon/telcon and Yeltsin/POTUS folder titles before broad policy files. Use broad chron and Situation Room files only to resolve missing contacts, source-note control, or chronology uncertainty.

sourceNoteModel.sourceStem: Source: William J. Clinton Presidential Library, Clinton Presidential Records, [collection or staff-file path], [series/file], OA/ID or OA/Box Number [number], [folder title or document control], [MDR/FOIA case or Clinton Digital Library item].
sourceNoteModel.frusPattern: Keep the displayed source note to repository, collection/control path, release/case locator, and face-page markings. Keep derivative-PDF extraction, page-count, search-history, and provenance-sheet audit prose in separate compiler notes.
requiredOnsiteAdditions: Confirm exact box/folder locator and whether the finding-aid OA/ID number is the call-slip control used in the research room.
Record folder title, collection, office/staff-file name, OA/ID, restrictions/withdrawal marker, and any declassification case number printed on the document.
For derivative PDFs, extract only the actual memcon or telcon pages and append the original source marker/provenance page as the final page.
Count actual conversation pages separately from marker pages, routing slips, talking points, briefing memoranda, and duplicate drafts.

onsiteWorkflow: Before arrival, print the six hard-source-gap map and this first-pull queue; convert the Tier A and B entries into call slips by OA/ID/folder title.
At the desk, confirm how Clinton Library staff want the 2013-0185-M OA/ID values translated into box/folder requests.
Day 1 should be direct folders only: Lake OA/ID 1466, Gati OA/ID 70/72, Medish OA/ID 2876/2877, Burns OA/ID 252/253, and the Gergen/Feeley telcon folders.
Day 2 should chase the six hard gaps through summit/trip books, Executive Secretary files, and Records Management trip books.
Day 3 should clean source notes with aide chron/notepads, Berger records of calls/schedules, POTUS Chron, Situation Room Logs, and Situation Room Summaries.
Only after actual memcon/telcon pages and withdrawal markers are controlled should the compiler spend time on GCC, NATO/Russia, arms-control, Kosovo, and speechwriting context files.
For every useful item, capture folder cover, marker/withdrawal sheet, document pages, and any stamp or declassification/control information. Record page counts before leaving the research room.
